TWO primary documents retrieved and read firsthand this session.

(A) T+1 close -> 05:15 SGT — SOLVED with an SGX-authored, SGX-hosted primary document (NOT the circular; the DT/AM circular remains unfound).
Document: "Derivatives Products Description", version 17.6, an SGX-authored Excel workbook (.xlsm inside a .zip) downloaded live from SGX's own file server. Its first sheet is "read_me", which carries a formal, columnar change log with headers at row 24: B="Issue Date (mm/dd/yyyy)", C="Version Number", D="Authors", E="Change Description". Every row's Authors cell reads "SGX". Issue dates are real Excel date serials, not free text.
Retrieved from: https://api2.sgx.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/Derivatives+Products+Description+v17.6 eff 20260824, 20260907.zip

(B) Japan T-session 14:25 -> 14:55 — the pointer's named document CONFIRMED by direct retrieval.
Document: SGX Circular No. DT/AM - 50 of 2024, dated 9 September 2024, "Extension of T-session for SGX Japan Derivatives and Intraday Margin Cycle 2 Timing Change", a 3-page SGX-letterhead PDF, verbatim, mirrored by member Fubon Futures via the Internet Archive.

verbatim:
=== (A) SGX "Derivatives Products Description" v17.6, sheet "read_me" — verbatim cell-by-cell ===
Source: https://api2.sgx.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/Derivatives+Products+Description+v17.6 eff 20260824, 20260907.zip

Column headers, row 24, verbatim:
  B24 = "Issue Date (mm/dd/yyyy)"
  C24 = "Version Number"
  D24 = "Authors"
  E24 = "Change Description"

The version 6.9 block, verbatim (rows 86-90; the Issue Date / Version / Authors cells sit on the LAST row of each bordered block):
  E86 = "Editorial housekeeping/standardisation contract name on Freight contracts"
  E87 = "Effective 11 Nov:"
  E88 = "Editorial change Contracts_mainmenu:"
  E89 = "(T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts"
  B90 = 43745  [Excel date serial = 2019-10-07]
  C90 = 6.9
  D90 = "SGX"
  E90 = "Editorial change session_mainmenu:
SURV_INT to 5:15, REMOVE_DAY_ORDERS to 5:20, SERIES_GEN to 5:22, 
CLS_CLEAR to 5:25 and CLOSE to 5:30 all T+1 traded contracts"

The immediately preceding block (v6.8) and following block (v7.0), verbatim, which bound the block and fix the year:
  E83 = "Effective 21 Oct:"
  E84 = "Amend, insert '4 Routes' in PV, PVF, CPV, PPV, CPVF, PPVF contract name"
  B85 = 43739 [2019-10-01]  C85 = 6.8  D85 = "SGX"  E85 = "Add PW, PWF, CPW, PPW, CPWF, PPWF"
  B91 = 43777 [2019-11-08]  C91 = 7.0  D91 = "SGX"  E91 = "Add MF5, MF5F, LSF, LSFF effective 18 Nov
Add VN & NVN effective 02 Dec"

The same change log's rows for the other SGX T+1/hours cutovers, verbatim (used as calibration, see notes):
  Issue 2023-10-26, v12.6, SGX: "Amend trading hours of US SSFs to reflect introduction of T+1 trading (eff 27 Nov)"
  Issue 2024-11-04, v14.2, SGX: "Amend trading hours of SGX Nikkei Derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures (eff 4 Nov)"
  Issue 2025-03-19, v14.9, SGX: "Amend T+1 session trading hours for SGX Equity Index Futures/ Options, Dividend Index Futures and United States Single Stock Futures (US SSFs) (eff 7 Apr)"
  Issue 2026-01-14, v16.6, SGX: "...Amend trading hours of TF, CTF, PTF to reflect introduction of T+1 trading (eff 26 Jan)"

Earlier "Effective <date>:" headers in the same log, verbatim, establishing that this is SGX's own recurring convention for scoping the lines that follow:
  Issue 2018-06-11, v4.5, SGX: "Effective 25 Jun: / Added NJY / Amend contract months for NK, NKO from 20Q to 32Q / ..."
  Issue 2018-07-03, v4.6, SGX: "Effective 23 July: / Added NMY, NPH, NTH / Removed CI, CIF / ..."
  Issue 2018-08-10, v4.7, SGX: "Effective 27 Aug: / Amended contract months for AC, ACF from 48 months, to up to 60 months / ..."
  Issue 2019-07-05, v6.4, SGX: "Effective 29 July: / Remove LN, LNF, NLN, NLNF, DLN, DLNF, PPS, PPSF, PES, PESF"

=== (B) SGX Circular No. DT/AM - 50 of 2024 — verbatim, extracted by me from the PDF ===
Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20241114183232/https://www.fubon.com/futures/wcm/home/bulletin/bulletin_20240912_137396/SGXChange.pdf

"Circular

9 September 2024

Circular No. DT/AM - 50 of 2024

Extension of T-session for SGX Japan Derivatives and Intraday
Margin Cycle 2 Timing Change

The Exchange would like to inform market participants that with effect from Monday, 4 November
2024, the T session trading hours for SGX Nikkei derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index
Futures will be extended by 30 minutes. This follows the decision of the Tokyo Stock Exchange Inc.
(TSE) to extend their trading hours from 5 November 2024, by 30 minutes to 3.30pm Japan
Standard Time1.

The Exchange will also be changing the timing for the intraday margin cycle 2 from 4.00pm to
5.00pm Singapore time with effect from Monday, 21 October 2024.

A. Extension of T Session Trading Hours
Effective Monday, 4 November 2024, the contracts for which T session trading hours will be
extended by 30 minutes are as follows:"
notes:
WHAT CHANGED VS THE POINTER. The pointer reported (A) unsolved and listed "SGX Derivatives Product Catalogue read_me change log" as already ruled out, on the grounds that "the text sits in a cell with no date, bound only by cell-border formatting". That ruling is incorrect, and (A) is now solved from that very artifact. I did not find the DT/AM circular for (A); that hunt stayed dead. What I found instead is a different SGX-authored primary document that states the effective day.

WHY THE EARLIER RULE-OUT WAS WRONG. Two objective, machine-readable facts in the file, both verified by parsing the OOXML directly rather than by looking at a rendering:
1. The change log IS dated. Sheet "read_me" has an explicit header row 24: B="Issue Date (mm/dd/yyyy)", C="Version Number", D="Authors", E="Change Description". The dates are genuine Excel date serials (e.g. 43745 = 2019-10-07), not formatting.
2. The block structure is encoded in the file, not merely visual. There are NO mergeCells in the sheet. Instead each multi-row version entry is a run of rows sharing explicit borderIds: borderId 2 = block top (top=thin, bottom=none), borderId 68 = block middle (no top, no bottom), borderId 67 = block bottom (bottom=thin) and that bottom row is the one carrying the Issue Date / Version / Authors cells. Single-row entries use borderId 1 (top and bottom both thin). Parsing those border ids gives an unambiguous partition. Rows 86,87,88,89,90 form exactly one block, terminating on row 90 which carries Issue Date 2019-10-07, Version 6.9, Author SGX. So "Effective 11 Nov:" (E87) and "(T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts" (E89) are inside the same SGX-dated version entry.

THE ANSWER FOR (A). Within v6.9, issued by SGX on 7 October 2019, the line "Effective 11 Nov:" heads the two lines that follow it, the second of which is "(T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts". 11 November 2019 was a Monday. The year is fixed with no room for doubt: the block is issued 2019-10-07 and the next block is issued 2019-11-08, so "11 Nov" can only be 11 November 2019.

THE ONE INTERPRETIVE STEP, STATED PLAINLY. SGX put the effective date in its own cell as a header ("Effective 11 Nov:") rather than inline in the same cell as the change. So the claim that the header scopes the following lines is a reading of SGX's layout, not a sentence SGX wrote as one string. I consider that reading safe, and here is why, but the maintainer should see it and decide:
 - It is SGX's own recurring convention, used in the same column across years, including v4.5 "Effective 25 Jun:", v4.6 "Effective 23 July:", v4.7 "Effective 27 Aug:", v6.4 "Effective 29 July:" and the immediately preceding block v6.8 "Effective 21 Oct:". In every one of those the header is followed by the items it governs, inside the same bordered block.
 - The alternative reading (that E87 governs nothing) would leave a dangling header, and would leave the largest session-time change in the workbook's history with no effective date at all, while trivia like multiplier changes all carry one.

CALIBRATION: THE SAME LOG IS RIGHT WHERE WE CAN CHECK IT. Three independent confirmations that this change log's "eff" dates are accurate operator records, not loose notes:
 - v14.2, issued 2024-11-04: "Amend trading hours of SGX Nikkei Derivatives and SGX FTSE Blossom Japan Index Futures (eff 4 Nov)". This is cutover (B), and it matches Circular DT/AM - 50 of 2024 exactly ("with effect from Monday, 4 November 2024"). The workbook independently reproduces a date we can prove from a real circular.
 - v14.9, issued 2025-03-19: "(eff 7 Apr)" for the T+1 session revision, matching Yuanta Futures bulletin 114A014 dated 2025/03/28 which states SGX changes T+1 hours from 2025/04/07.
 - v12.6, issued 2023-10-26: "(eff 27 Nov)" for US SSF T+1 introduction, matching the 27 Nov 2023 item the earlier sweep found at Trading Technologies.
So for (B) the workbook and the circular agree, which is the strongest available evidence that the workbook is trustworthy for (A), where no circular survives.

THE 04:45 INTERMEDIATE STEP: STILL UNSOURCED, AND NOW POSITIVELY DOUBTFUL. I searched every shared string in the workbook. There is exactly one "4:45" anywhere in it, and it is a T+1 OPEN time, not a close: "(T) 9:00am -4:35pm / (T+1) 4:45pm - 5:15am". SGX's own change log records the T+1 CLOSE moving to 5:15am exactly ONCE, in v6.9 eff 11 Nov 2019, and contains no entry moving a T+1 close to 04:45 at any point from the workbook's first version (2016-02-19) onward. That does not disprove an intermediate step, but it means SGX's own product-parameter record shows a single move, and the "04:45 on the 2019-05-31 SGX page" observation should be re-examined before a 04:45 row is written. Consider that a 4:45pm T+1 open may have been misread as an 04:45 close.

WHAT DID NOT WORK FOR (A), ADDING TO THE POINTER'S DEAD ENDS.
 - The DT/AM circular for the 2019 T+1 extension: still not found anywhere. SGX does host DTAM circulars on its own server (confirmed live: DTAM 87 of 2024, DTAM 24 of 2025, DTAM 64 of 2023, DTAM 93 of 2023, DTAM 67 of 2022 all return HTTP 200 at api2.sgx.com/sites/default/files/YYYY-MM/), but nothing from 2019 is present on the server or in the Wayback CDX. Wayback's coverage of api2.sgx.com is thin: the whole domain yields only ~5,241 distinct URLs, of which 239 are under files/2019 and none is a circular.
 - Brute-forced api2.sgx.com for 2019-era editions of the workbook itself (2019-10, 2019-11, 2019-12, 2020-01 x v6.9/v7.0 x xlsm/zip/xls, both "+" and space naming): all 404. Only the two 2025 editions (v16.3, v16.4) plus the current v17.6 are archived or live. So the contemporaneous 2019 edition is not retrievable; the change log is however cumulative and carried forward intact by SGX.
 - SGX's Drupal content API (https://api2.sgx.com/content-api?queryId=<hash>:page&variables={"path":...}) accepts arbitrary paths with a known persisted-query id, but /derivatives/circulars, /regulation/circulars and /membership/circulars all return {"data":{"route":null}} — SGX publishes no circulars index at those paths.
 - Taiwanese broker bulletins are the broker's own words with no SGX attachment. I pulled Yuanta Futures 114A014 in full (https://www.yuantafutures.com.tw/UploadFile/Artical/202503/1743137570645_114A014.pdf); it is a Yuanta-letterhead summary table, no SGX circular attached. Useful only as calibration, never as a source. Fubon's live /bulletin/doc/SGXJPXTimechange.pdf returns an HTML shell, not a PDF; only the Internet Archive copy of the dated /bulletin_YYYYMMDD_NNNNNN/ folder works.
 - KGI Securities Singapore: Wayback CDX over the whole kgieworld.sg domain (60,000 URLs) surfaces only 8 SGX-related PDFs, all factsheets/agreements, nothing from 2019 and no circular besides the 2020 FTSE one the earlier sweep already had.

RECOMMENDATION FOR THE REPO. Cite (A) to the SGX workbook change log, quoting v6.9 / Issue Date 2019-10-07 / "Effective 11 Nov:" / "(T+1) session Closing hours to 5:15am all T+1 traded contracts", with the effective day recorded as Monday 2019-11-11, and note in the row's provenance that the effective date is a block header rather than an inline clause. Cite (B) to Circular DT/AM - 50 of 2024 for Monday 2024-11-04. Do NOT write a 04:45 row on current evidence. Because SGX overwrites this workbook in place at a new monthly URL each release, archive the exact file: sha256 bbc3b60e22a3b62fe0d9ee56b3249d5171332992bc73474a80476d116c8b69ce.
